articles.headline: NVIDIA Reports Record Data Center Revenue Amid AI Boom
articles.summary: NVIDIA's data center revenue surged 409% year-over-year as demand for AI chips continues to outpace supply. The company raised guidance for the upcoming quarter.
articles.body:
NVIDIA Corporation reported record-breaking quarterly results, with data center revenue reaching $18.4 billion, up 409% from the same period last year. CEO Jensen Huang attributed the growth to unprecedented demand for AI infrastructure.

The company's H100 and upcoming H200 GPUs remain in high demand across cloud providers and enterprises building AI capabilities. "We are seeing demand from every industry vertical," Huang said during the earnings call.

NVIDIA raised its Q2 guidance above analyst expectations, projecting revenue of $24 billion. The stock rose 8% in after-hours trading.

articles.headline: Apple Unveils Vision Pro 2 with Enhanced AI Features
articles.summary: Apple announced the next generation of its spatial computing headset with improved display technology and native AI capabilities powered by Apple Intelligence.
articles.body:
Apple Inc. unveiled Vision Pro 2 at a special event today, featuring a 40% lighter design and enhanced AI capabilities. The new headset includes an updated M4 chip optimized for spatial computing and real-time AI processing.

Key features include improved pass-through cameras, longer battery life of up to 4 hours, and deep integration with Apple Intelligence for real-time translation, object recognition, and contextual assistance.

The Vision Pro 2 will be available starting at $2,999, down from the original's $3,499 price point. Pre-orders begin February 15.

articles.headline: Federal Reserve Signals Potential Rate Cut in March
articles.summary: Fed Chair Powell indicated the central bank is prepared to begin cutting rates if inflation continues its downward trajectory, boosting equity markets.
articles.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell signaled today that the central bank may begin cutting interest rates as early as March if inflation data continues to show improvement.

"We have made considerable progress toward our 2% inflation target," Powell said in prepared remarks. "The committee is gaining confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward our goal."

Markets responded positively, with the S&P 500 rising 0.8% following the comments. Financial stocks led gains as lower rates typically boost lending activity.

articles.headline: Tesla Faces Increased Competition in China EV Market
articles.summary: Tesla's market share in China declined for the third consecutive quarter as domestic competitors BYD and Nio gain ground with more affordable models.
articles.body:
Tesla Inc. reported a 15% decline in China deliveries for Q4 2025, marking the third consecutive quarter of market share losses in the world's largest EV market.

BYD, which surpassed Tesla as the world's largest EV maker by volume, continues to gain share with its competitively priced Seal and Dolphin models. Nio has also seen strong growth with its battery-swap technology appealing to range-anxious consumers.

Tesla responded by cutting prices on Model 3 and Model Y in China by up to 6%, but analysts say more aggressive action may be needed. "Tesla needs to accelerate its next-generation vehicle platform to remain competitive," said Dan Levy at Barclays.

articles.headline: Microsoft Azure Revenue Growth Accelerates on AI Demand
articles.summary: Microsoft reported Azure cloud revenue growth of 31%, beating estimates as enterprises accelerate AI adoption through its OpenAI partnership.
articles.body:
Microsoft Corporation reported stronger-than-expected cloud results, with Azure revenue growing 31% year-over-year, up from 28% in the previous quarter.

CEO Satya Nadella attributed the acceleration to AI workloads, particularly through the company's partnership with OpenAI. "We're seeing customers move from AI experimentation to production deployments," Nadella said.

The company's AI services, including Copilot for Microsoft 365, contributed approximately 6 percentage points to Azure growth. Enterprise customers are increasingly adopting the $30/month Copilot add-on for productivity software.

articles.headline: Amazon Expands Same-Day Delivery to 15 New Markets
articles.summary: Amazon announced expansion of its same-day delivery service to 15 additional metropolitan areas, intensifying competition with Walmart and Target.
articles.body:
Amazon.com Inc. announced today that it will expand same-day delivery service to 15 new metropolitan areas by the end of Q1 2026, bringing total coverage to over 100 markets.

The expansion is part of Amazon's ongoing logistics investments, which totaled over $60 billion in 2025. The company has built out a network of smaller fulfillment centers closer to population centers to enable faster delivery.

"Customer expectations continue to rise, and we're investing to meet them," said Doug Herrington, CEO of Worldwide Amazon Stores. The move puts additional pressure on competitors Walmart and Target, which have been expanding their own same-day capabilities.

articles.headline: Eli Lilly's GLP-1 Drug Sales Exceed $10B Quarterly
articles.summary: Eli Lilly reported quarterly sales of Mounjaro and Zepbound exceeded $10 billion combined, beating estimates as the company expands manufacturing capacity.
articles.body:
Eli Lilly and Company reported blockbuster results for its GLP-1 medications, with combined sales of Mounjaro (for diabetes) and Zepbound (for weight loss) reaching $10.2 billion in Q4 2025.

The results easily beat analyst estimates of $9.1 billion, driven by strong demand and improved manufacturing capacity. CEO David Ricks said supply constraints that plagued the drugs in 2024 have been largely resolved.

"We're now able to meet patient demand in most markets," Ricks said. The company expects GLP-1 revenue to grow another 40% in 2026 as it expands into new indications including sleep apnea and heart failure.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Drop as OPEC+ Considers Production Increase
articles.summary: Crude oil fell 3% on reports that OPEC+ members are discussing increasing production quotas amid concerns about demand growth.
articles.body:
Oil prices dropped sharply today on reports that OPEC+ is considering increasing production quotas at its upcoming meeting. Brent crude fell 3.2% to $78.45 per barrel, while WTI declined 3.5% to $73.20.

Sources familiar with the discussions said Saudi Arabia is facing pressure from other members to relax production cuts that have been in place since 2023. The kingdom has been shouldering a disproportionate share of cuts to support prices.

Energy stocks underperformed, with Exxon Mobil and Chevron both declining over 1%. Analysts at Goldman Sachs maintained their year-end Brent target of $85, citing resilient global demand.

articles.headline: Meta Launches New AI Research Lab in London
articles.summary: Meta Platforms announced a new AI research facility in London, committing $500 million to hire 200 researchers focused on multimodal AI systems.
articles.body:
Meta Platforms Inc. announced plans to establish a major AI research laboratory in London, investing $500 million over three years. The facility will focus on multimodal AI systems that can process and generate text, images, and video.

The lab will employ approximately 200 researchers and engineers, with hiring expected to begin immediately. Meta cited London's strong academic institutions and diverse talent pool as key factors in the decision.

"London has become a global hub for AI talent," said Yann LeCun, Meta's Chief AI Scientist. "This investment underscores our commitment to fundamental AI research." The move comes as competition for AI talent intensifies among tech giants.

articles.headline: Boeing Reaches Settlement with DOJ Over 737 MAX Cases
articles.summary: Boeing agreed to pay $2.5 billion to settle remaining Department of Justice claims related to the 737 MAX crashes, removing a major legal overhang.
articles.body:
Boeing Company reached a comprehensive settlement with the Department of Justice to resolve remaining criminal charges related to the 737 MAX crashes that killed 346 people in 2018 and 2019.

The $2.5 billion settlement includes $1.8 billion in compensation to victim families, $500 million in fines, and $200 million for safety improvements. Boeing also agreed to enhanced oversight of its safety processes.

"This settlement allows us to focus fully on rebuilding trust and delivering safe aircraft," said Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg. The stock rose 2% in pre-market trading as investors viewed the settlement as removing significant legal uncertainty.

articles.headline: Google Cloud Partners with Deutsche Bank on AI Transformation
articles.summary: Alphabet's Google Cloud announced a multi-year partnership with Deutsche Bank to modernize the bank's technology infrastructure using AI.
articles.body:
Google Cloud announced a strategic partnership with Deutsche Bank valued at approximately $1 billion over five years. The deal will see Deutsche Bank migrate significant workloads to Google Cloud and adopt AI-powered tools for risk management and customer service.

"This partnership will accelerate our digital transformation," said Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing. The bank plans to use Google's Vertex AI platform to enhance fraud detection and automate compliance processes.

The deal is Google Cloud's largest in the financial services sector and represents a significant win against AWS and Azure in the competitive enterprise cloud market.

articles.headline: Pfizer Announces Positive Phase 3 Results for RSV Vaccine
articles.summary: Pfizer reported successful Phase 3 trial results for its RSV vaccine in older adults, potentially adding another revenue stream to offset COVID-19 vaccine decline.
articles.body:
Pfizer Inc. announced positive results from a Phase 3 clinical trial of its RSV vaccine candidate, showing 89% efficacy in preventing severe respiratory infections in adults over 60.

The results position Pfizer to compete with GSK's Arexvy, currently the only FDA-approved RSV vaccine for older adults. The RSV vaccine market is projected to reach $10 billion annually by 2030.

"These data support a strong efficacy and safety profile," said Pfizer's Chief Scientific Officer. The company plans to file for FDA approval in Q2 2026, with potential launch by late 2026.

articles.headline: Netflix Subscriber Growth Beats Expectations on Password Crackdown Success
articles.summary: Netflix added 15 million subscribers in Q4, well above estimates, as its password-sharing crackdown and ad-tier continue to drive growth.
articles.body:
Netflix Inc. reported subscriber additions of 15.2 million in Q4 2025, crushing analyst estimates of 11 million. The company now has 295 million global subscribers.

The strong results were driven by continued benefits from the password-sharing crackdown initiated in 2023, as well as growing adoption of the ad-supported tier, which now represents 45% of new signups in markets where it's available.

"We're seeing sustainable growth across all regions," said co-CEO Greg Peters. The company raised prices in several markets and announced plans to expand its live events programming, including exclusive NFL games in 2026.

articles.headline: JPMorgan Acquires Fintech Startup for $2B
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase announced the acquisition of payments fintech Plaid competitor for $2 billion, expanding its digital banking capabilities.
articles.body:
JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced a $2 billion acquisition of Lynk, a fintech startup that provides open banking and payment connectivity solutions. The deal expands JPMorgan's capabilities in account aggregation and real-time payments.

Lynk processes over 500 million API calls monthly, connecting 10,000 banks and financial institutions. The acquisition is JPMorgan's largest fintech deal since acquiring digital bank Nutmeg in 2021.

"Open banking is transforming how consumers interact with financial services," said JPMorgan's head of consumer banking. The deal is expected to close in Q2 2026, subject to regulatory approval.

articles.headline: Intel Announces Major Restructuring, 10,000 Job Cuts
articles.summary: Intel unveiled a sweeping restructuring plan including 10,000 layoffs and the sale of its NAND memory business as it focuses on AI and foundry services.
articles.body:
Intel Corporation announced a major restructuring plan including approximately 10,000 job cuts, representing about 10% of its workforce. The company will also divest its NAND memory business to SK Hynix for $7 billion.

CEO Pat Gelsinger said the moves are necessary to fund Intel's ambitious foundry expansion plans. "We must focus our resources on our core processor and foundry businesses," he said.

The restructuring will result in $3 billion in annual cost savings by 2027. Intel also announced it had won a major U.S. government contract worth $5 billion to produce advanced chips domestically under the CHIPS Act.
